newsitem.title: GERMANY: "Fair trade" coffee campaigners defend scheme.
newsitem.headline: "Fair trade" coffee campaigners defend scheme.

text.p: Historically high coffee prices are no reason to abandon calls for "fairly-priced" revenue structures for smallholders and co-operatives, the press spokesman of a German campaign said.

"Most Central American crops were sold ahead of the current price rallies at 140-150 cents/lb," said Harald Gruber of the German TransFair project from a Munich gathering of aligned producers and roasters.
"The farmer does not fully participate in the explosive gains seen in recent weeks."
Arabica futures on Monday plummeted on speculative liquidation after a dramatic run-up to 20 year highs last week, which resulted from global tightness and took prices above $3.00/lb.
The TransFair project sells coffee under fair-trade labels, based on guaranteed returns at 126 cents/lb, plus additional revenue in line with retail price averages of the day.
Retail prices of TransFair coffees were currently at around 11.50-12.00 marks per 500 grams of roasted coffee, Gruber said.
The "fair coffee" meeting this week will discuss scope for organically grown coffee and minimum environmental standards.
It is made up of 100 representatives of growers and licencees in the German project, the multi-country Dutch Max Havelaar Foundation and the British Fairtrade organisation.
The three groups together sold 11,000 tonnes of roasted coffee in 1996.
